subject: Myth & Symbolism
subcategory: The World Tree and Cosmic Maps
title: The Flat Earth and Its Edge
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Flat Earth and Its Edge usable.

hook.text: Ancient Greeks knew the earth was round. But many cultures imagined edges, walls, and waterfalls at the world's rim.

buildup.text: Norse myth placed a sea at the world's edge where Jörmungandr circled. Hindu cosmology ringed the earth with oceans.

discovery.text: The disc-world image survived into medieval art. Mappa Mundi showed a flat circle with Jerusalem at the center.

twist.text: The myth that medieval people believed in a flat earth is itself a myth. The real flat-earthers are modern.

climax.text: Edges give shape to the world. Without a boundary, there's no inside. The edge makes the center meaningful.

punchline.text: The edge isn't real. The fear of it is.

quiz.question: Did most medieval scholars believe the earth was flat?
options: No, most educated people knew it was round
